proposed.text: A structural engineer proposes a minimum design roof wind load of 95 kg/m² for a school building in a low-wind-hazard municipality. Per PD 1096, Rule XII, Section 1206, is this compliant?

options.text: Yes — local wind hazard surveys may reduce the minimum below 120 kg/m², provided they are approved by the local building official
No — the minimum is 150 kg/m² for educational occupancies, as specified in the national building code
No — Section 1206 requires a minimum of 120 kg/m² regardless of location or occupancy type
Yes — Section 1206 applies only to buildings taller than 3 storeys, allowing flexibility for smaller structures

Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: This provision reflects the Philippines' national vulnerability to typhoons. Even buildings in nominally 'low-wind' areas must resist at least 120 kg/m² — a baseline protection against under-designed roofs in typhoon years. The NSCP wind maps may require substantially more in actual typhoon corridors.
